planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring so roots establish before summer heat, siting them in humus-rich, evenly moist, acidic, well-drained soil with some shelter from harsh afternoon sun.

directions: A Broken Arrow Nursery selection of Japanese clethra, chosen for inflorescences that run up to 8 inches long, noticeably larger and more heavily branched than those of typical seedling-grown plants, opening fragrant white flowers in July. Like the species, it carries attractive cinnamon-brown, exfoliating bark that becomes a strong winter feature as the plant ages, and its rich green summer foliage turns orange and bronze in autumn. Candelabra is vigorous and tolerates pruning well, allowing it to be trained into a small specimen tree rather than left as a multi-stemmed shrub. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to shelter the foliage from the harshest afternoon sun, and prune to shape right after flowering since next year's buds form on new wood.
